subject: Feedback from Console as an reactive output? Or way to report progress

messages.author: 2b2736921b464c6e
messages.subject: Feedback from Console as an reactive output? Or way to report progress
parts:
Hi there, I've just started using Shiny, and enjoying it so far :)

However, I have a little problem - I'm trying to use Shiny as a dashboard using the Google Analytics API.  I have had success preloading the API calls in the global.R script for fixed queries, but I now want to make the API calls respond to user's input via Shiny's ui.R.

Depending on the date ranges and the metrics/dimensions a user puts in, this could take quite a long time to query the API, especially for rollups that may involve ~200 calls to GA API.

Doing this in RStudio is fine, as the API script writes to the console, giving user feedback, but for Shiny Server I don't know how to output this info whilst a user is waiting.  This will also help debugging the board :)

Are there any tips for the above? If I could just dump what I normally see in RStudio console whilst running the functions into a reactive output that would be great (and useful anyhow for other things), or if the print calls used in the function runs could be outputted as the function runs that may be better? It would also be nice for making progress bars for any functions that will take a long time.

Yours faithfully,
Mark

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Feedback from Console as an reactive output? Or way to report progress
parts:
Sorry, we don't currently have a good answer for this, unless you know a little HTML/JavaScript. You can have your shinyServer function take a "session" param: (function (input, output, session) )

and then in your server.R you can make calls like this:

session$sendCustomMessage("progress", list(
  completed = completedUnits / totalUnits,
  message = progressMessage
))

In your ui.R you can inject some JavaScript that does something like this:

Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("progress", function(data) {
  // Do something with data.completed and data.message
});

Now you have a connection between the server and the client; you could use some JavaScript to actuate a Twitter Bootstrap progress bar, for example.

(Eventually this will all get wrapped up nice in a bow for you so you don't need to do any custom JS of your own, but since progress probably needs to be pretty flexible, it's not something that we have had time to do just yet.)
